title: Build VM core memory and addressing modes
lead: Implement the ISA types in `internal/isa` and, in `internal/vm`, the circular core of CORESIZE cells with modulo addressing, the last-writer id, and operand evaluation for every addressing mode, test-first with Go table-driven tests and a fuzz target.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** opcode execution, process queues, placement, scheduling, any I/O.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Milestone 2 (VM core with unit tests per opcode and addressing mode). Every other package reads and writes cells through this layer. The core must be pure (C12) and deterministic (C36).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/isa/isa.go`: `Opcode`, `Modifier`, `Mode` types with constants in spec order, `Cell` (opcode, modifier, A and B operands with modes, last-writer id), and exported slices listing every opcode, modifier and mode (used by later enumeration tests).
- `internal/isa/isa_test.go`: the lists have no duplicates and match the constants.
- `internal/vm/core.go`: `Core` (fixed-size cell slice), constructor filling the spec's empty cell, address normalization, read and write (write records the bot id).
- `internal/vm/operand.go`: operand evaluation for every addressing mode.
- `internal/vm/core_test.go`, `internal/vm/operand_test.go`: table-driven tests.
- `internal/vm/fuzz_test.go`: `FuzzResolve` with a seed corpus.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestAddressingModes`: one table row per addressing mode, taken from the ISA spec's worked cases, each row named by its mnemonic (`t.Run(mnemonic, ...)`).
- `TestWrap`: addresses 0, CORESIZE-1, CORESIZE, -1 and large negative offsets normalize per the spec, for at least core sizes 1, 8 and 8000.
- `TestWriteRecordsWriter`: a write sets the cell's last-writer id; a read does not change it.
- `TestEmptyCore`: a fresh core holds the spec's empty-cell value at every address.
- `FuzzResolve`: for any core size in the spec's range, any operand value and any mode, the resolved address is in [0, CORESIZE) and evaluation does not panic.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
- Pure packages: no I/O, clock, goroutines or randomness (C12); no maps (C36).
- Choose integer types so modulo arithmetic is exact and cannot overflow for any allowed CORESIZE; one normalization function used everywhere.
- The exported API (type and function names, error handling) is the implementer's call, recorded per C35.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `. scripts/env.sh && go test ./... && go vet ./... && test -z "$(gofmt -l cmd internal)"` passes.
- `. scripts/env.sh && go test -run '^$' -fuzz FuzzResolve -fuzztime 30s ./internal/vm` finds no failure.
- Each addressing mode in the spec has a named subtest (`go test -v -run TestAddressingModes ./internal/vm` lists one per mnemonic).
- Purity: `. scripts/env.sh && go list -f '{{join .Imports "\n"}}' ./internal/isa ./internal/vm | grep -xE 'os|os/.*|io|io/.*|net|net/.*|time|math/rand|math/rand/v2|sync|sync/.*|syscall|log|log/.*|unsafe'` prints nothing.
- No maps: `grep -rn --include='*.go' --exclude='*_test.go' 'map\[' internal/vm` prints nothing.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Branch `slice/<id>-vm-memory` in `.worktrees/<id>`. One commit when the owner asks.
